To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the micromagnetic simulation of magnetoelectric systems requires the introduction of an additional interaction term in the energy functional and that the micromagnetics software Nmag can be extended to simulate such systems.

magnetoelectric materials can be simulated by an extension of the micromagnetic model that parallels the introduction of the spin-current interaction term and that this extension can be implemented in the micromagnetic software package Nmag.
micromagnetic simulation of magnetoelectric coupling can be performed using a simple extension to the Nmag software.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical simulation of magnetoelectric effects in micromagnetic systems.

the development of numerical methods for micromagnetic simulations of “magneto-electric materials”, i.e. systems that show magnetoelectric coupling, i.e. an interaction between electric polarization and magnetic order.
the development and use of computational micromagnetics as a tool for studying magnetization dynamics and magnetoelectricity in magnetic materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the micromagnetic model for magnetoelectric materials is a well defined extension of the standard model, which has been implemented in a widely used micromagnetic simulator.
the magnetoelectric coupling in the micromagnetic model can be treated in a straightforward manner by adding the appropriate terms to the energy functional.
the magnetoelectric interaction is a new and exciting phenomenon in magnetism that has been predicted to occur in a variety of different materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to simulate the micromagnetic response of a magnetoelectrics system to an external electric field.
the magnetoelectric interaction can be treated in Nmag in a similar way as spin-currents are treated in Nmag.
we can now simulate the dynamics of magnetoelectric systems with Nmag.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the micromagnetic model can be extended to describe the magnetoelectric coupling of materials that show an electric polarization that is coupled to an inhomogeneous magnetostatic field.
magnetoelectric effects can be simulated using standard micromagnetic software packages with only minor modifications to the code.
the magnetoelectric interaction can be treated as a simple addition of a new term to the usual micromagnetic equations, and the numerical implementation of this term is not particularly complicated.
